content.title: LaMelo Ball gets real about Hornets Play-In loss, season end: 'It hurts a lot'
content.text: From earning his first career All-Star selection to enduring a frustrating bench role at the end of the season, Norman Powell saw a roller-coaster 2025-26 outing in Miami. The Miami Heat are facing major questions heading into a highly important offseason this year, and one of the key components they have to address is their future with Norman Powell. As such, while he enjoyed being a part of the team, Powell appeared noncommittal about the idea of staying in South Beach and running it back with the Heat. "You know, you can want things and stuff like that, but it's all about what makes the most sense. I enjoyed my time here in Miami. I've always wanted to play for the Heat," Powell said in his exit interview this season for Miami. "I thought it was a good year for me in spite of the injuries and some of the setbacks and stuff like that, but I enjoyed my time." "I enjoyed the staff and my teammates and everything that came along with the season. I thought we had a great time off the court, really bonding and being able to joke around and things like that, and that's the most important part about the season is the bonds and stuff that you make." Powell arrived in Miami from the Los Angeles Clippers in last year's offseason. Under head coach Erik Spoelstra, Powell enjoyed the biggest break of his career by earning his first-ever NBA All-Star nod and becoming the team's first option. But in the final stretch of the season, a groin injury disturbed Powell's momentum, causing him to miss 13 consecutive games. Upon rejoining the Heat, he struggled and was subsequently demoted to the bench. Powell is set to become a free agent with an expiring $20.4 million contract. More than anything else and what might await his next cotract status, the star swingman is cherishing the bond and relationship he built in Miami. "You know, every season there's only one champion, so it's all about the memories and things that you make and the ups and downs and going through it, and I thought we had a great team that stuck together and enjoyed the ups and downs and just bonding on and off the court," Powell concluded.
